verdict.rationale: Homebrew ships its own bulk operations. `brew bundle` installs every dependency declared in a Brewfile with a single command, and `brew bundle dump` snapshots all installed packages at once. `brew untap` removes one or more taps, `brew autoremove` cleans up unneeded dependencies, and `brew upgrade` (with `--greedy` for casks) updates everything; community reports confirm `brew upgrade` acts on all packages at once. Missing for 10: explicit docs for multi-argument install/uninstall of arbitrary named items, filter- or selection-based bulk targeting, and documented dry-run previews beyond `brew bundle check`.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: It allows you to tell users to run a single command to install all dependencies for a project and start any services.
`Brewfile`s can also be used as a way of saving all supported packages into a single file.
brew untap <user>/<repository> [...] removes one or more taps.
Uninstall formulae that were only installed as a dependency of another formula and are now no longer needed.
use `brew upgrade --greedy` if you want Homebrew to update them too.
